title.zh: 卷三百七十六 列傳第一百三十五 常同 張致遠 薛徽言 陳淵 魏矼 潘良貴 呂本中
title.en: Volume 376 Biographies 135: Chang Tong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Xue Huiyan, Chen Yuan, Wei Gang, Pan Lianggui, Lu Benzhong
title.raw: 卷三百七十六 列傳第一百三十五 常同 張致遠 薛徽言 陳淵 魏矼 潘良貴 呂本中 Volume 376 Biographies 135: Chang Tong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Xue Huiyan, Chen Yuan, Wei Gang, Pan Lianggui, Lu Benzhong

sentences.zh: 常同 張致遠 薛徽言 陳淵 魏矼 潘良貴 呂本中

translations.literal: Chang Tong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Xue Huiyan, Chen Yuan, Wei Gang, Pan Lianggui, and Lu Benzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Xue Huiyan, Chen Yuan, Wei Gang, Pan Lianggui, and Lu Benzhong.

sentences.zh: 常同，字子正，邛州臨邛人，紹聖御史安民之子也。

translations.literal: Chang Tong, courtesy name Zizheng, was a native of Linqiong in Qiongzhou, and was the son of Anmin, a censor of the Shaosheng era.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong, styled Zizheng, came from Linqiong in Qiong Prefecture. He was the son of Chang Anmin, who had served as a censor under Emperor Zhezong in the Shaosheng reign.

sentences.zh: 登政和八年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: In 1118 he took the highest civil-service degree.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，除大理司直，以敵難不赴，辟元帥府主管機宜文字，尋除太常博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang period he was appointed Directing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, but because of the enemy crisis he did not take up the post; he was then recruited as drafter for confidential matters on the staff of the Marshal's Office, and soon after was made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin crisis broke in 1126, he was named a reviewing clerk in the Court of Judicial Review but never reported, owing to the invasion. Instead he joined the marshal's headquarters as a policy secretary and was soon made an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，辟浙帥機幕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong crossed south, Tong was recruited onto the military staff of the Zhejiang commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's flight south, he entered the secretariat of the Zhejiang military command.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，詔：“故監察御史常安民、左司諫江公望，抗節剛直，觸怒權臣，擯斥至死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan an edict said: "The late Investigating Censor Chang Anmin and Left Remonstrator Jiang Gongwang, in their upright integrity and firmness, offended powerful ministers and were driven out until death.
translations.idiomatic: In 1130 the throne issued an edict: "The late Investigating Censor Chang Anmin and Left Remonstrator Jiang Gongwang stood on principle with unbending integrity, provoked the wrath of powerful ministers, and were hounded from office to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 今其子孫不能自振，朕甚憫之。”

translations.literal: Now their descendants cannot lift themselves up; We are deeply moved with pity."
translations.idiomatic: Their descendants have been unable to recover their standing, and We are deeply grieved for them."

sentences.zh: 召同至行在，至則為大宗丞。

translations.literal: Tong was summoned to the mobile court, and on arrival was made Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong was summoned to the imperial camp; when he arrived he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，乞郡，得柳州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he requested a prefectural post and was given Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 he asked to leave the capital for a prefecture and was sent to Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，召還，首論朋黨之禍：“自元豐新法之行，始分黨與，邪正相攻五十年。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled and first discussed the calamity of faction: "From the time the New Policies of the Yuanfeng era were implemented, factions began to be formed, and the wicked and the upright attacked one another for fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: In 1133 he was recalled and opened with a memorial on the scourge of partisan politics: "Ever since the New Policies of the Yuanfeng era, courtiers have split into factions; for fifty years the righteous and the corrupt have torn one another apart.

sentences.zh: 章惇唱於紹聖之初，蔡京和于崇寧之後，元祐臣僚，竄逐貶死，上下蔽蒙，豢成夷虜之禍。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun took the lead at the beginning of Shaosheng, and Cai Jing chimed in after Chongning; the officials of the Yuanyou era were banished, degraded, and put to death; above and below were blinded, and the disaster of the barbarian invaders was nurtured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun led the charge at the start of Shaosheng; Cai Jing took up the chorus after Chongning. Yuanyou ministers were exiled, demoted, and killed until the court was hoodwinked top to bottom—and the barbarian catastrophe was bred in that darkness.

sentences.zh: 今國步艱難，而分朋締交、背公死黨者，固自若也。

translations.literal: Now the nation's step is perilous, yet those who form factions, bind alliances, turn their backs on the public good, and die for their clique remain as they were.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is in grave peril, yet men still form cliques, weave private alliances, betray the public good, and die for their party as before.

sentences.zh: 恩歸私門，不知朝廷之尊；

translations.literal: Favor returns to private households, and they do not know the honor due the court;
translations.idiomatic: Patronage flows into private gates while the majesty of the throne is forgotten;

sentences.zh: 重報私怨，寧復公議之顧。

translations.literal: they set great store by repaying private grudges and would rather abandon regard for public deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: private vengeance weighs heavier than public deliberation.

sentences.zh: 臣以為欲破朋黨，先明是非，欲明是非，先辨邪正，則公道開而奸邪息矣。”

translations.literal: Your servant holds that to break factions one must first clarify right and wrong; to clarify right and wrong one must first distinguish the wicked from the upright—then the path of public fairness opens and treachery ceases."
translations.idiomatic: I believe that to shatter factionalism we must first settle what is true and what is false; to settle truth and falsehood we must first separate the corrupt from the upright. Then the public way will open and wickedness will wither.

sentences.zh: 上曰：“朋黨亦難破。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Factions are also hard to break."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "Partisan blocs are not easily broken."

sentences.zh: 同對：“朋黨之結，蓋緣邪正不分，但觀其言行之實，察其朋附之私，則邪正分而朋黨破矣。”

translations.literal: Tong replied: "The knotting of factions arises because the wicked and the upright are not distinguished; only observe the reality of their words and deeds and scrutinize the private motives of their clique-attachments, and the wicked and the upright will be separated and the factions broken."
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong answered, "Factions form because no one distinguishes the wicked from the upright. Judge men by what they actually say and do, expose the private interests behind their alliances, and the righteous will stand apart from the corrupt—then the factions collapse."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“君子小人皆有黨。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Gentlemen and petty men alike have parties."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Noble men and petty men alike have their followings."

sentences.zh: 同又對曰：“君子之党，協心濟國；

translations.literal: Tong replied again: "The party of the gentleman joins hearts to aid the state;
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong replied again, "A gentleman's faction unites in heart to serve the realm;

sentences.zh: 小人之黨，挾私害公。

translations.literal: the party of the petty man embraces private interest to harm the public good.
translations.idiomatic: a petty man's faction hugs private interest and harms the public good.

sentences.zh: 為黨則同，而所以為黨則異。

translations.literal: In forming a party they are the same, but in what they form a party for they differ.
translations.idiomatic: Both are called parties, yet what they party for is utterly different.

sentences.zh: 且如元祐臣僚，中遭讒謗，竄殛流死，而後禍亂成。

translations.literal: Take, for example, the officials of the Yuanyou era: midway they suffered slander, were banished, executed, and exiled to death, and afterward calamity and disorder arose.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Yuanyou ministers: midway they were slandered, exiled, executed, and left to die in banishment—and only afterward did catastrophe engulf the realm.

sentences.zh: 今在朝之士，猶謂元祐之政不可行，元祐子孫不可用。”

translations.literal: Now among those at court there are still some who say that Yuanyou policies cannot be carried out and that the descendants of Yuanyou cannot be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Even now some at court still insist that Yuanyou policies must never be revived and that the sons and disciples of Yuanyou must never be used.

sentences.zh: 上曰：“聞有此論。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have heard that there is such talk."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I have heard such talk."

sentences.zh: 同對以：“禍亂未成，元祐臣僚固不能以自明。

translations.literal: Tong replied: "Before calamity and disorder had taken shape, the officials of Yuanyou naturally could not clear themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong replied, "Before the disasters struck, Yuanyou men could not clear their own names.

sentences.zh: 今可謂是非定矣，尚猶如此，蓋今日士大夫猶宗京、黼等傾邪不正之論。

translations.literal: Now it may be said that right and wrong are settled, yet it is still like this—because today's scholar-officials still adhere to the crooked and unrighteous doctrines of men such as Jing and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Today right and wrong are settled beyond doubt, yet the court still behaves this way—because many scholar-officials still cling to the warped doctrines of men like Cai Jing and Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 朋黨如此，公論何自而出？

translations.literal: When factions are like this, from where can public deliberation emerge?
translations.idiomatic: With factionalism like this, how can honest public debate ever rise?

sentences.zh: 願陛下始終主張善類，勿為小人所惑。”

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to uphold the good consistently from beginning to end and not be deluded by petty men.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to stand by the good from first to last, and not let petty men lead you astray."

sentences.zh: 又奏：“自古禁旅所寄，必參錯相制。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "From antiquity the forces entrusted to the palace guard have always been deployed in mixed and mutually restraining arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial: "Since antiquity, the troops entrusted to the inner guard have always been posted in overlapping, mutually checking formations.

sentences.zh: 漢有南北軍，周勃用南軍入北軍以安劉氏，唐李晟亦用神策軍以復京師，是其效也。

translations.literal: Han had the Northern and Southern Armies; Zhou Bo used the Southern Army to enter the Northern Army and thereby secure the Liu house; in Tang, Li Sheng likewise used the Shence Army to recover the capital—such was their effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Han had Northern and Southern Armies; Zhou Bo marched the Southern Army into the Northern Army and thereby saved the Liu dynasty. In Tang, Li Sheng used the Shence Army to retake Chang'an—the same lesson.

sentences.zh: 今國家所仗，惟劉光世、韓世忠、張俊三將之兵耳。

translations.literal: What the state now relies on is only the armies of the three generals Liu Guangshi, Han Shizhong, and Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Today the dynasty relies on the armies of only three generals: Liu Guangshi, Han Shizhong, and Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 陛下且無心腹禁旅，可備緩急，頃者苗、劉之變，亦可鑒矣。”

translations.literal: Your Majesty moreover has no trusted inner guard that can meet an emergency; the recent Miao and Liu mutiny may also serve as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty still has no trusted inner guard ready for sudden crisis—the recent Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan mutiny should be warning enough."

sentences.zh: 除殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Attending Censor within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 時韓世忠屯鎮江，劉光世屯建康，以私忿欲交兵。

translations.literal: At that time Han Shizhong was encamped at Zhenjiang and Liu Guangshi at Jiankang; because of private resentment they wished to fight one another.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Han Shizhong held Zhenjiang and Liu Guangshi Jiankang; private grievances nearly brought their armies to blows.

sentences.zh: 同奏：“光世等不思待遇之恩，而驕狠尚氣，無所忌憚，一旦有急，其能相為唇齒乎？

translations.literal: Tong memorialized: "Guangshi and the others do not think on the grace of their treatment, but are arrogant, fierce, and honor spirit; they have nothing they fear—once there is urgency, can they act as lip and teeth for one another?
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong memorialized, "Guangshi and his peers forget the grace shown them. Arrogant and violent, they answer to nothing but their own pride. In a crisis, will they stand shoulder to shoulder?

sentences.zh: 望分是非，正國典。

translations.literal: I hope to distinguish right and wrong and rectify the statutes of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Distinguish right from wrong and enforce the law of the land.

sentences.zh: 昔漢諸侯王有過，猶責師傅，今兩軍幕屬贊畫無狀，乞先黜責。”

translations.literal: In former times when Han feudal princes had faults, their tutors were still punished; today the staff of the two armies who planned and abetted them behaved without propriety—I beg that they be dismissed and punished first."
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, when a feudal prince erred, his tutors were punished. Today the staff who egged on both armies have behaved disgracefully—I beg that they be dismissed and punished first."

sentences.zh: 上以章示兩軍。

translations.literal: The emperor showed the memorial to both armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had the memorial shown to both armies.

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩再相，同論其十事，且曰：“陛下未欲遽罷頤浩者，豈非以其有復辟之功乎？

translations.literal: When Lu Yihao became chief minister again, Tong criticized him on ten points and said: "If Your Majesty does not wish to dismiss Yihao immediately, is it not because he has the merit of restoring the throne?
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Yihao returned as chief minister, Chang Tong laid out ten charges against him and said, "If Your Majesty hesitates to remove Yihao at once, is it not because he claims credit for restoring the throne?

sentences.zh: 臣謂功出眾人，非一頤浩之力。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the merit came from the multitude of men, not from Yihao's strength alone.
translations.idiomatic: That achievement belonged to many men, not to Yihao alone.

sentences.zh: 縱使有功，宰相代天理物，張九齡所謂不以賞功者也。”

translations.literal: Even if he had merit, the chief minister stands in for Heaven to order all things—what Zhang Jiuling called not rewarding merit."
translations.idiomatic: Even if he had merit, a chief minister governs on Heaven's behalf—as Zhang Jiuling said, one does not reward merit in such an office."

sentences.zh: 頤浩罷相。

translations.literal: Yihao was dismissed from the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 論知樞密院宣撫川陝張浚喪師失地，遂詔浚福州居住。

translations.literal: He criticized Zhang Jun, who as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Pacification Commissioner for Chuan and Shaanxi had lost his army and territory; an edict then ordered Jun to reside in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Zhang Jun, Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi, for losing troops and territory; the court ordered Jun to reside in Fuzhou in exile.

sentences.zh: 同與辛炳在台同好惡，上皆重之。

translations.literal: Tong and Xin Bing at the Censorate shared likes and dislikes, and the emperor valued them both.
translations.idiomatic: At the Censorate, Chang Tong and Xin Bing thought alike on matters of right and wrong, and the Emperor esteemed them both.

sentences.zh: 金使李永壽等入見，同言：“先振國威，則和戰常在我；

translations.literal: When the Jin envoy Li Yongshou and others were received in audience, Tong said: "First rouse the nation's prestige, and peace or war will constantly rest with us;
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin envoy Li Yongshou and others were received, Chang Tong said, "First restore the nation's prestige, and whether we fight or negotiate will remain in our hands;

sentences.zh: 若一意議和，則和戰常在彼。”

translations.literal: if we devote ourselves solely to discussing peace, then peace or war will constantly rest with them."
translations.idiomatic: if we fix our minds only on peace talks, peace and war will rest in theirs."

sentences.zh: 上因語及武備曰：“今養兵已二十萬。”

translations.literal: The emperor, turning the talk to military preparedness, said: "We now maintain an army of two hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, turning to armaments, said, "We now keep two hundred thousand troops under arms."

sentences.zh: 同奏：“未聞二十萬兵而畏人者也。”

translations.literal: Tong memorialized: "I have never heard of two hundred thousand troops yet fearing others.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong replied, "I have never heard of an army of two hundred thousand that still trembles before the enemy."

sentences.zh: 偽齊宿遷令張澤以二千人自拔來歸，泗州守徐宗誠納之，韓世忠以聞。

translations.literal: The Suqian magistrate of the puppet Qi, Zhang Ze, came over to the Song of his own accord with two thousand men; the prefect of Sizhou, Xu Zongcheng, accepted them, and Han Shizhong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ze, magistrate of Suqian under the puppet Qi regime, defected with two thousand men. Xu Zongcheng, prefect of Sizhou, received them, and Han Shizhong reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 朝論令世忠卻澤等，而械宗誠赴行在。

translations.literal: Court opinion ordered Shizhong to send Ze and the others back, and to send Zongcheng in fetters to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: The court majority ordered Han Shizhong to turn Zhang Ze's men away and to send Xu Zongcheng to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 同奏：“敵雖議和，而兩界人往來未嘗有禁，偽齊尚能置歸受館，立賞以招吾民，今乃卻澤，人心自此離矣。

translations.literal: Tong memorialized: "Although the enemy is discussing peace, travel between the two borders has never been forbidden; the puppet Qi could still set up reception halls for defectors and offer rewards to lure our people—yet now we turn Ze away, and hearts will from this depart.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong objected: "Though the enemy talks of peace, people still cross the border freely. Even the puppet Qi set up halls to receive defectors and posted rewards to lure our subjects—yet we would turn Zhang Ze away and lose hearts from that hour.

sentences.zh: 況宗誠起土豪，不用縣官財賦，募兵自養，為國障捍，今因受澤而械之，以沮士氣，非策也。”

translations.literal: Moreover Zongcheng rose from a local strongman, did not use county tax revenues, raised troops to support himself, and shielded the state—now because he received Ze he is put in fetters, which will dampen morale; this is not a good policy."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zongcheng was a local magnate who raised and fed his own troops without draining the county treasury and held the frontier for the state. To clap him in irons for accepting defectors will crush morale. That is no policy at all."

sentences.zh: 詔處來歸者於淮南，釋宗誠罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that those who came over be settled in Huainan, and Zongcheng's offense was released.
translations.idiomatic: An edict settled the defectors in Huainan and pardoned Xu Zongcheng.

sentences.zh: 四年，除起居郎、中書舍人、史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Gentleman Attendant, Secretariat Drafter, and Compiler of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaoxing he was made Gentleman Attendant, Secretariat Drafter, and Compiler of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 先是，同嘗上疏論神、哲二史曰：“章惇、蔡京、蔡卞之徒積惡造謗，痛加誣詆，是非顛倒，循致亂危。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tong had submitted a memorial on the Veritable Records of Shenzong and Zhezong, saying: "Men such as Zhang Dun, Cai Jing, and Cai Bian heaped up evil and fabricated slander, bitterly adding false denunciations; right and wrong were inverted, and step by step disorder and peril were brought on.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chang Tong had memorialized on the Veritable Records of Shenzong and Zhezong: "Zhang Dun, Cai Jing, Cai Bian, and their ilk piled up crimes and forged slanders, heaping false charges until truth and falsehood were reversed and calamity followed step by step.

sentences.zh: 在紹聖時，則章惇取王安石《日錄》私書改修《神宗實錄》；

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng period Zhang Dun took Wang Anshi's private letters, the Diary, and revised the Veritable Records of Shenzong;
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaosheng, Zhang Dun took Wang Anshi's private Diary and reworked the Veritable Records of Shenzong;

sentences.zh: 在崇甯後，則蔡京盡焚毀《時政記》、《日曆》，以私意修定《哲宗實錄》。

translations.literal: after Chongning, Cai Jing burned the Political Records and the Daily Calendar entirely and revised the Veritable Records of Zhezong according to private intent.
translations.idiomatic: after Chongning, Cai Jing burned the Political Records and Daily Calendar wholesale and redrafted the Veritable Records of Zhezong to suit himself.

sentences.zh: 其間所載，悉出一時奸人之論，不可信於後世。

translations.literal: What is recorded in them all came from the opinions of wicked men of that time and cannot be trusted by later ages.
translations.idiomatic: What those books contain is nothing but the talk of villains of the hour—no later age should trust them.

sentences.zh: 恭惟宣仁保佑之德，豈容異辭，而蔡確貪天之功，以為己力，厚誣聖後，收恩私門。

translations.literal: Reverently considering the protecting and preserving virtue of Empress Xuanren, how could variant wording be tolerated? Yet Cai Que greedily took Heaven's merit as his own strength, grossly slandered the sage empress, and gathered favor into private gates.
translations.idiomatic: The protecting grace of Empress Xuanren brooks no second telling, yet Cai Que stole Heaven's credit for himself, grossly defamed the sage empress, and hoarded favor for his own house.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位之初，嘗下詔明宣仁安社稷大功，令國史院摭實刊修，又復悠悠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's accession an edict was once issued clarifying Xuanren's great merit in securing the altars of state and ordering the Historiography Institute to select facts and publish a revision—yet again it drifted on without result.
translations.idiomatic: At Your Majesty's accession you once issued an edict proclaiming Xuanren's great service to the realm and ordered the Historiography Institute to compile the truth—yet the work again drifted unfinished.

sentences.zh: 望精擇史官，先修《哲宗實錄》，候書成，取《神宗朱墨史》考證修定，庶毀譽是非皆得其實。”

translations.literal: I hope to select historians with care, first revise the Veritable Records of Zhezong, and when that book is complete take the Vermilion-and-Ink History of Shenzong, verify it, and revise it, so that praise and blame, right and wrong, may all obtain their reality."
translations.idiomatic: Choose historians with care, revise the Veritable Records of Zhezong first, then when that is done collate the Vermilion-and-Ink History of Shenzong and set the record straight, so that praise and blame may finally match the truth."

sentences.zh: 上深嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor warmly approved.

sentences.zh: 至是，命同修撰，且諭之曰：“是除以卿家世傳聞多得事實故也。”

translations.literal: At this time he was ordered to serve as co-compiler, and was also instructed: "This appointment is because your family's transmitted hearsay over generations has obtained many facts."
translations.idiomatic: Now he was ordered to serve as co-compiler and told, "You are appointed because your family has handed down much that is factual."

sentences.zh: 一日奏事，上愀然曰：“向昭慈嘗言，宣仁有保佑大功，哲宗自能言之，正為宮中有不得志于宣仁者，因生誣謗。

translations.literal: One day while reporting on affairs the emperor said with a somber look: "Formerly Zhaoci once said that Xuanren had a great merit of protection and preservation, and Zhezong himself could speak of it—it was just that in the palace there were those who had not achieved their ambitions under Xuanren, and so slander arose.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as he reported on business, the Emperor said gravely, "Empress Zhaoci once told me that Xuanren had guarded the throne with great merit, and that Zhezong himself could have said so. Slander arose only because palace people who had not prospered under her nursed grievances.

sentences.zh: 欲辨白其事，須重修《實錄》，具以保立勞效，昭示來世，此朕選卿意也。”

translations.literal: To clarify the matter one must revise the Veritable Records, fully set forth the labor and effect of her protection and establishment, and display it to later generations—this is the meaning of My selecting you."
translations.idiomatic: To clear her name the Veritable Records must be rewritten, her labors in protecting the dynasty set forth in full, and shown to posterity. That is why I chose you."

sentences.zh: 同乞以所得聖語宣付史館，仍記於《實錄》卷末。

translations.literal: Tong requested that the imperial words he had received be proclaimed and delivered to the Historiography Institute and still recorded at the end of the Veritable Records volume.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong asked that these imperial words be promulgated to the Historiography Institute and copied at the end of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 張俊乞復其田產稅役，令一卒持書瑞昌，而淩悖其令郭彥參，彥參系之獄。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun requested restoration of his fields, produce, and tax corvée; he sent one soldier with a letter to Ruichang, but the soldier insulted and defied the magistrate Guo Yancan, and Yancan put him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhang Jun petitioned to restore his landholdings and tax exemptions and sent a soldier with his letter to Ruichang. The man insulted and defied the magistrate Guo Yancan, who threw him in jail.

sentences.zh: 後訴於朝，命罷彥參，同並封還二命。

translations.literal: Later he appealed to the court; an order dismissed Yancan, and Tong together returned both edicts sealed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun appealed to court; the throne ordered Guo Yancan's dismissal, but Chang Tong returned both edicts unapproved.

sentences.zh: 俄除集英殿修撰、知衢州，以疾辭，除徽猷閣待制、提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Talents and prefect of Quzhou; citing illness he declined, and was made Awaiting Draft at the Huaiyou Pavilion and Commissioner for the Jizhou Taiping Taoist Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Talents and prefect of Quzhou; pleading illness, he was instead made Awaiting Draft at the Huaiyou Pavilion and put in charge of the Taiping Taoist Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，以禮部侍郎召還。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未數日，除御史中丞。

translations.literal: Within a few days he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 車駕自建康回臨安，同奏：“旋蹕之初，去淮益遠，宜遣重臣出按兩淮，詢人情利病，察官吏侵擾，縱民耕墾，勿收租稅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned from Jiankang to Lin'an, Tong memorialized: "At the beginning of the turn back from the imperial progress, we are farther from the Huai than before; it is fitting to send a weighty minister to inspect the Two Huai, inquire into popular feelings, benefits, and harms, investigate official oppression, and let the people plow and open land without collecting rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved back from Jiankang to Lin'an, he memorialized: "As the throne turns homeward we drift farther from the Huai. Send a senior minister to tour the Two Huai, learn what the people suffer and need, punish predatory officials, and let farmers reclaim fields without rent or tax for now.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，田野加辟，百姓足而國亦足矣。”

translations.literal: After several years the fields will be increasingly opened, the common people will be sufficient and the state also sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: In a few years the land will widen under the plow, the people will be fed, and the treasury will follow."

sentences.zh: 乃遣樞密使王庶視師，同乞以此奏付庶，詢究罷行。

translations.literal: The court then sent Grand Councilor Wang Shu to inspect the armies; Tong requested that this memorial be given to Shu, who inquired into it and then stopped carrying it out.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Grand Councilor Wang Shu to inspect the armies. Chang Tong asked that this memorial be handed to Wang Shu, who investigated it and then let the plan drop.

sentences.zh: 又言：“江浙困于月樁錢，民不聊生。”

translations.literal: He also said: "Jiang and Zhe are distressed by the monthly assessment money, and the people have no means of livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Jiangsu and Zhejiang are crushed by the monthly assessment levy; the people can barely live."

sentences.zh: 上為減數千緡。

translations.literal: The emperor reduced it by several thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor cut the levy by several thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 又言：“吳

translations.literal: He also said: "Wu
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Wu

sentences.zh: 玠屯師興、利，而西川人力已困。

translations.literal: Jie has his army stationed in Xing and Li, while the manpower of western Sichuan is already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Jie holds his army in Xing and Li prefectures, yet the manpower of western Sichuan is already spent.

sentences.zh: 玠頃年嘗講屯田，願聞其積穀幾何，減饋運幾何，趙開、李迨相繼為都漕，先後饋運各幾何，令制、漕、帥司條具以聞，然後按實講究，以紓民力。”

translations.literal: In recent years Jie once discussed garrison farming; I wish to hear how much grain was accumulated and how much transport of provisions was reduced; Zhao Kai and Li Dai successively served as overall transport commissioners—how much was transported provisionally in each case?—order the pacification, transport, and command offices to list items and report, and afterward verify in fact and discuss, so as to ease the people's strength."
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Jie promoted garrison farming. How much grain did he store? How much supply transport did he cut? Zhao Kai and Li Dai served in turn as overall transport commissioners—how much did each ship? Let the pacification, transport, and command offices report item by item; then verify the figures and ease the people's burden."

sentences.zh: 又言：“國家養兵，不為不多，患在於偏聚而不同力，自用而不同心。

translations.literal: He also said: "The state maintains troops—not a few; the trouble lies in their being gathered in separate concentrations and not combining strength, each using his own and not sharing one heart.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The state keeps no small army, yet the armies cluster in separate camps—they do not combine their strength, and each general minds only himself.

sentences.zh: 今韓世忠在楚，張俊在建康，岳飛在江州，吳玠在蜀，相去隔遠，情不相通。

translations.literal: Now Han Shizhong is in Chu, Zhang Jun at Jiankang, Yue Fei at Jiangzhou, and Wu Jie in Shu; they are far apart and their feelings do not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong holds Chu, Zhang Jun Jiankang, Yue Fei Jiangzhou, Wu Jie Sichuan—far apart, hearts not speaking to hearts.

sentences.zh: 今陛下遣樞臣王庶措置邊防，宜令庶會集將帥，諭以國體，協心共議禦敵，常令諸軍相接以常山蛇勢，一意國家，無分彼此，緩急應援，皆有素定之術。”

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has sent the councilor Wang Shu to arrange the border defense; it is fitting to order Shu to assemble the commanders, instruct them in the body of the state, join hearts to deliberate together on resisting the enemy, constantly keep the armies in contact in the Constant Mountain Snake formation, with one intent for the state and no division into self and other, so that in urgency or ease mutual rescue all have settled methods."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has sent Wang Shu to arrange the frontier. Let Shu gather the commanders, teach them what the realm requires, and make them plan together against the enemy. Keep the armies linked like the Constant Mountain Snake of the Art of War—one will for the state, no 'mine' and 'yours'—so that in crisis or calm relief has a settled plan."

sentences.zh: 詔付王庶出示諸將。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that it be given to Wang Shu to show the generals.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the memorial handed to Wang Shu to show the generals.

sentences.zh: 同乞郡，除顯謨閣直學士、知湖州。

translations.literal: Tong requested a prefectural post and was appointed Direct Academician at the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong asked for a prefecture and was made Direct Academician at the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 復召，請祠，詔提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: He was recalled again, requested a Taoist abbey commission, and was ordered to serve as Commissioner for the Jiangzhou Taiping Taoist Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled again, he asked for a sinecure and was ordered to oversee the Taiping Taoist Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十年卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Shaoxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1150.

sentences.zh: 張致遠

translations.literal: Zhang Zhiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiyuan

sentences.zh: 張致遠，字子猷，南劍州沙縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhiyuan, courtesy name Ziyou, was a native of Shaxian in Nanjian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiyuan, styled Ziyou, was from Shaxian in Nanjian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，中進士第。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1121 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 宰相范宗尹薦其才，召對，擢為樞密院計議官。

translations.literal: Chief minister Fan Zongyin recommended his talent; he was summoned to audience and was promoted to Planning Officer of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Fan Zongyin recommended his talent; summoned to audience, he was raised to Planning Officer in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 建寇範汝為已降，猶懷反側，而招安官謝向、陸棠受賊賂，陰與之通。

translations.literal: The Jian bandit Fan Ruwei had already surrendered but still harbored wavering intent, while the pacification officers Xie Xiang and Lu Tang accepted bribes from the bandits and secretly communicated with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jian bandit Fan Ruwei had surrendered but still wavered toward revolt, while pacification officers Xie Xiang and Lu Tang took bribes and dealt with him in secret.

sentences.zh: 致遠謁告歸，知其情，還白執政，請鋤其根枿，於是捕響、棠及制置司屬官施宜生付獄。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan took leave to return home, learned the situation, returned and reported to the chief ministers, and requested to uproot the roots; thereupon Xiang, Tang, and Shi Yisheng, a subordinate of the Pacification Commission, were arrested and put in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan went home on leave, learned the truth, returned to warn the chief ministers, and urged that the roots be cut. Xie Xiang, Lu Tang, and Pacification Commission clerk Shi Yisheng were arrested and jailed.

sentences.zh: 詔參知政事孟庾為福州宣撫使討賊，韓世忠副之，辟致遠為隨軍機宜文字。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Participating Administrator Meng Geng Pacification Commissioner of Fuzhou to suppress the bandits, with Han Shizhong as his deputy; Zhiyuan was recruited as drafter for confidential matters accompanying the army.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Participating Administrator Meng Geng Pacification Commissioner of Fuzhou to crush the rebels, with Han Shizhong as his deputy, and recruited Zhiyuan as army policy secretary.

sentences.zh: 賊平，除兩浙轉運判官，改廣東轉運判官。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified he was appointed Transport Intendant of the Two Zhe circuits, then changed to Transport Intendant of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were pacified he was made Transport Intendant for the Two Zhes, then for Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 招撫劇盜曾兗等，賊眾悉降。

translations.literal: He pacified and recruited the fierce bandits Zeng Yan and others, and the bandit hosts all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the fierce bandit Zeng Yan and others until their whole host surrendered.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，以監察御史召。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing he was summoned as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1134 he was summoned as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 未至，除殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was appointed Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could arrive he was made Attending Censor within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 時江西帥胡世將請增和買絹折納錢，致遠上疏言：“折納絹錢本欲少寬民力，而比舊增半，是欲乘民之急而厚其斂也。”

translations.literal: At that time the Jiangxi commander Hu Shijiang requested an increase in the cash commutation for harmonized-purchase silk, and Zhiyuan submitted a memorial saying: "The cash commutation for silk was originally meant to ease the people's strength somewhat, but compared with the old quota it is increased by half—this is to take advantage of the people's urgency and thicken the levy."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangxi commander Hu Shijiang asked to raise the cash commutation for state silk purchases. Zhang Zhiyuan memorialized: "The commutation fee was meant to lighten the people's load, yet this proposal raises it half again above the old rate—that is to squeeze the people harder when they are already desperate."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his memorial.

sentences.zh: 金人與劉豫分道入寇，宰相趙鼎勸高宗親征，朝士尚以為疑，白鼎審處。

translations.literal: The Jin people and Liu Qi invaded by separate routes; Chancellor Zhao Ding urged Emperor Gaozong to lead the campaign in person; officials at court still had doubts and told Ding to handle the matter carefully.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin and Liu Qi struck by separate routes, Chancellor Zhao Ding urged Gaozong to take the field in person. Many at court still hesitated and asked Ding to proceed with caution.

sentences.zh: 致遠入對，獨贊其決。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan entered for audience and alone praised this decision.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiyuan alone, in audience, endorsed the decision.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 言：“聚財養兵，皆出民力，善理財者，宜固邦本。

translations.literal: He said: "Gathering wealth to maintain troops all comes from the people's strength; those skilled at managing finances should consolidate the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Armies are fed from the people's labor. A good treasurer must strengthen the state's foundation.

sentences.zh: 請罷榷福建鹽，精擇三司使、副，以常平茶鹽合為一官，令計經常，量入為出，先務省節，次及經理。”

translations.literal: I request abolishing the Fujian salt monopoly, carefully selecting the Commissioner and Vice Commissioner of the Three Departments, combining the Ever-Normal Granary with tea and salt into one office, ordering calculation of regular revenues, measuring outgo by income, first striving for economy, and next for management."
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the Fujian salt monopoly. Choose the Three Departments commissioners with care. Merge the Ever-Normal Granary with the tea-and-salt office, set regular budgets, match spending to income, economize first, then manage what remains."

sentences.zh: 詔戶部講究。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Ministry of Revenue to study the proposal.

sentences.zh: 五年，除戶部侍郎，進吏部侍郎，尋復為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, advanced to Vice Minister of Personnel, and soon again made Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he was made Vice Minister of Revenue, then Vice Minister of Personnel, and soon returned to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 言：“陛下欲富國強兵，大有為於天下，願詔大臣力務省節，明禁僭侈，自宮禁始，自朝廷始。

translations.literal: He said: "Your Majesty wishes to enrich the state and strengthen the army and accomplish great things under Heaven; I beg that Your Majesty order the great ministers to strive forcefully for economy, clearly forbid extravagance, beginning with the palace precincts and beginning with the court.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Your Majesty wishes to enrich the state, strengthen the army, and achieve great things. Order your chief ministers to practice strict economy, forbid extravagance plainly, and begin with the palace and the court itself.

sentences.zh: 額員可減者減之，司屬可並者並之。

translations.literal: Where established quotas can be reduced, reduce them; where subordinate offices can be merged, merge them.
translations.idiomatic: Cut quotas where they can be cut; merge offices where they can be merged.

sentences.zh: 使州縣無妄用，歸其餘于監司；

translations.literal: Let prefectures and counties spend nothing recklessly and return the surplus to the supervisory commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: Let prefectures and counties spend nothing without cause and return surpluses to the circuit commissioners;

sentences.zh: 監司無妄用，歸其餘於朝廷；

translations.literal: let the commissioners spend nothing recklessly and return the surplus to the court;
translations.idiomatic: let commissioners return their surpluses to the court;

sentences.zh: 朝廷無橫費，日積月聚，惟軍須是慮，中興之業可致也。”

translations.literal: let the court have no reckless expenditures, accumulating day by day and month by month, with only military needs in view—then the work of restoration can be attained."
translations.idiomatic: let the court spend nothing without need, hoard month by month for the army alone—and restoration will be within reach."

sentences.zh: 除給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Drafting Recipient.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Drafting Recipient.

sentences.zh: 尋以老母丐外，以顯謨閣待制知台州。

translations.literal: Soon, citing his aged mother, he requested an outside post and was made Awaiting Draft at the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he begged leave to care for his aged mother and was made Awaiting Draft at the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以海寇鄭廣未平，改知福州。

translations.literal: Because the sea bandit Zheng Guang had not yet been pacified, the court changed his appointment to prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because the pirate Zheng Guang was still at large, he was transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，廣等降，致遠選留四百人，置營城外，餘遣還業。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year Guang and others surrendered; Zhiyuan selected four hundred men to remain, set up a camp outside the city wall, and sent the rest back to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year Zheng Guang surrendered. Zhiyuan kept four hundred men in a camp outside the walls and sent the rest home to their trades.

sentences.zh: 復遣廣討他郡諸盜，數月悉平。

translations.literal: He again sent Guang to suppress bandits in other prefectures, and within several months all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Guang to hunt bandits in neighboring prefectures; within months all were subdued.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，再召為給事中。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he was again summoned as Drafting Recipient.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year he was recalled as Drafting Recipient.

sentences.zh: 出知廣州。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以顯謨閣待制致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Awaiting Draft at the Xianmo Pavilion and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he retired with the title Awaiting Draft at the Xianmo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 十七年卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year of Shaoxing, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 致遠鯁亮有學識，曆台省、侍從，言論風旨皆卓然可觀。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan was upright and bright, with learning; passing through the Censorate and the inner court, his words and aims were all outstanding and worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiyuan was upright, learned, and bright. Through the Censorate and the inner court his speeches and policies were consistently admirable.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎嘗謂其客曰：“自鼎再相，除政府外，從官如張致遠、常同、胡寅、張九成、潘良貴、呂本忠、魏矼皆有士望，他日所守當不渝。”

translations.literal: Zhao Ding once told his guests: "Since Ding became chief minister again, apart from the government, the attendant officials such as Zhang Zhiyuan, Chang Tong, Hu Yin, Zhang Jiucheng, Pan Lianggui, Lu Benzhong, and Wei Gang all enjoy scholarly repute; what they uphold in days to come should not waver."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding once told his clients, "Since I returned as chief minister, the attendant officials—Zhang Zhiyuan, Chang Tong, Hu Yin, Zhang Jiucheng, Pan Lianggui, Lu Benzhong, Wei Gang—enjoy real standing. Their constancy in years ahead should not waver."

sentences.zh: 識者謂鼎為知人雲。

translations.literal: Men of discernment said that Ding knew men.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said Ding knew how to judge men.

sentences.zh: 薛徽言

translations.literal: Xue Huiyan
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huiyan

sentences.zh: 薛徽言，字德老，溫州人。

translations.literal: Xue Huiyan, courtesy name Delao, was a native of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huiyan, styled Delao, was from Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，為樞密院計議官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was made Planning Officer of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and became a Planning Officer in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，遣使分行諸路，徽言在選中，以權監察御史宣諭湖南。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing envoys were dispatched to tour the various circuits; Huiyan was among those selected and, as Acting Investigating Censor, was sent to proclaim and instruct Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1132 the court sent envoys to tour the circuits. Huiyan was chosen and, as Acting Investigating Censor, sent to proclaim the throne's will in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時郴、道、桂陽旱饑，徽言請於朝，不待報即諭漕臣發衡、永米以振，而以經制銀市米償之，所刺舉二十人。

translations.literal: At that time Chen, Dao, and Guiyang suffered drought and famine; Huiyan requested of the court and, without awaiting reply, ordered the transport commissioner to release Heng and Yong grain for relief, using regulated-funds silver to buy grain for repayment, and impeached twenty men.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, Dao, and Guiyang were stricken by drought and famine. Huiyan petitioned the court, then—without waiting for a reply—ordered the transport commissioner to release grain from Heng and Yong for relief, using regulated-funds silver to buy replacement grain, and impeached twenty officials.

sentences.zh: 使還，他使皆進擢，宰相呂頤浩以徽言擅易守臣，而移用經制銀，出知興國軍。

translations.literal: When he returned from his mission, the other envoys were all advanced in rank; Chief Minister Lü Yihao, because Huiyan had on his own authority replaced a guarding prefect and diverted regulated-funds silver, sent him out as prefect of the Xingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the other envoys were promoted, but Lü Yihao, angered that Huiyan had replaced a prefect on his own authority and spent regulated funds, sent him out to command the Xingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 入為郎、遷右司，擢起居舍人。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as a bureau director, was transferred to the Right Office, and was promoted to Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a bureau director, moved to the Right Office, and was raised to Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時秦檜與金人議和，徽言與吏部侍郎晏敦復等七人同拜疏爭之。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Hui was negotiating peace with the Jin; Huiyan together with Vice Minister of Personnel Yan Dunfu and six others jointly submitted a memorial opposing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui was negotiating peace with the Jin, Huiyan joined Vice Minister Yan Dunfu and six others in a joint memorial of protest.

sentences.zh: 一日，檜於上前論和，徽言直前引義固爭，反復數刻。

translations.literal: One day, as Hui was arguing for peace before the emperor, Huiyan stepped forward, cited principle, and firmly contested it, back and forth for several quarters of an hour.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as Hui argued for peace before the throne, Huiyan stepped forward, cited principle, and disputed him back and forth for nearly an hour.

sentences.zh: 中寒疾而卒。

translations.literal: He died of a chill contracted in the midst of it.
translations.idiomatic: He caught a chill in the debate and died.

sentences.zh: 高宗念之，賻絹百匹，特與遺表恩。

translations.literal: The emperor thought of him and granted one hundred bolts of silk as funeral gifts, with special favor for his final memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong mourned him, granted a hundred bolts of silk, and gave special favor to his final memorial.

sentences.zh: 陳淵，字知默，南劍州沙縣人也。

translations.literal: Chen Yuan, courtesy name Zhimò, was a native of Shaxian in Nanjian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuan, styled Zhimò, was from Shaxian in Nanjian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，給事中廖剛、中書舍人胡寅朱震、權戶部侍郎張致遠言：“淵乃瓘之諸孫，有文有學，自瓘在時，器重特甚，垂老流落，負材未試。”

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Drafting Recipient Liao Gang, Secretariat Drafter Hu Yin, Zhu Zhen, Acting Vice Minister of Revenue Zhang Zhiyuan said: "Yuan is a grandson of Chen Guan, literate and learned; when Guan was alive he was especially valued, and now in old age he drifts in neglect, his talent untested."
translations.idiomatic: In 1135 Liao Gang, Hu Yin, Zhu Zhen, and Zhang Zhiyuan memorialized: "Chen Yuan is a grandson of Chen Guan—learned and capable. Guan prized him highly; now in his old age he drifts unemployed, his talent untried."

sentences.zh: 充樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會李綱以前宰相為江南西路安撫制置大使，辟為制置司機宜文字。

translations.literal: When Li Gang, as former chief minister, became Pacification and Military Commissioner of the Jiangxi West Circuit, Yuan was recruited as drafter for confidential matters on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang, the former chief minister, became Pacification Commissioner for Jiangxi West, Yuan joined his staff as policy secretary.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔侍從舉直言極諫之士，胡安國以淵應。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered attendant officials to recommend men of forthright speech and extreme remonstrance; Hu Anguo nominated Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the throne ordered attendants to recommend blunt remonstrators; Hu Anguo nominated Yuan.

sentences.zh: 召對，改官，賜進士出身。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, his rank was changed and he was granted jinshi standing.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he was given a new rank and granted jinshi standing.

sentences.zh: 九年，除監察御史，尋遷右正言。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Investigating Censor and soon transferred to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Investigating Censor, then Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 入對，論：“比年以來，恩惠太濫，賞給太厚，頒賚賜予之費太過。

translations.literal: Entering for audience he discussed: "In recent years favors have been too lavish, rewards too generous, and the costs of distributions, grants, and gifts too great.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said, "In recent years imperial favor has run too wide, rewards too rich, and the cost of grants and gifts too heavy.

sentences.zh: 所用既眾，而所入實寡，此臣所甚懼也。

translations.literal: What is spent is many, while what comes in is truly few—this is what your servant greatly fears.
translations.idiomatic: Outgo is vast while income is thin—that is what I most fear.

sentences.zh: 《周官》‘唯王及後、世子不會’，說者謂不得以有司之法治之，非周公作法開後世人主侈用之端也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou say 'only the king, the queen, and the heir apparent are not subject to accounting'; commentators hold that they cannot be governed by the statutes of the regular offices—this is not the Duke of Zhou making law to open the way for later rulers to spend lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou says only the king, queen, and heir are 'not subject to accounting.' Commentators take that to mean they escape ordinary fiscal law—not that the Duke of Zhou opened the door for later rulers to spend without limit.

sentences.zh: 臣謂塚宰以九式均節財用，有司雖不會，塚宰得以越式而論之。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the Grand Steward, by the nine formulas, balances and regulates finances; though the regular offices do not account for the throne, the Grand Steward may still exceed the formulas in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Steward balances revenue by the nine formulas. Though the regular offices do not audit the throne, the Grand Steward may still judge spending against those formulas.

sentences.zh: 若事事以式，雖不會猶會也。

translations.literal: If in every matter one follows the formulas, though there is no accounting it is still accounting.
translations.idiomatic: If every grant were weighed by formula, the throne would be accounted for in all but name.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下凡有錫賚，法之所無而於例有疑者，三省得以共議，戶部得以執奏，則前日之弊息矣。”

translations.literal: Your servant hopes that whenever Your Majesty has gifts and grants for which the law has nothing and precedent is doubtful, the Three Departments may deliberate together and the Ministry of Revenue may memorialize and remonstrate—then the abuses of former days will cease.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that whenever Your Majesty grants what the law does not cover and precedent doubts, the Three Departments debate together and Revenue remonstrate—then yesterday's abuses will end."

sentences.zh: 淵面對，因論程頤、王安石學術同異，上曰：“楊時之學能宗孔、孟，其《三經義辨》甚當理。”

translations.literal: Yuan faced the emperor and thereupon discussed whether the learning of Cheng Yi and Wang Anshi was the same or different; the emperor said: "Yang Shi's learning can take Confucius and Mencius as its lineage; his Exegesis of the Three Classics is very much in accord with principle."
translations.idiomatic: In audience Yuan compared the learning of Cheng Yi and Wang Anshi. The Emperor said, "Yang Shi's learning follows Confucius and Mencius; his Exegesis of the Three Classics is sound."

sentences.zh: 淵曰：“楊時始宗安石，後得程顥師之，乃悟其非。”

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Shi at first took Wang Anshi as his master; afterward he obtained Cheng Hao as teacher and then understood his error."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "Yang Shi first followed Wang Anshi; only after studying under Cheng Hao did he see the error."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“以《三經義解》觀之，具見安石穿鑿。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Judging from the Exegesis of the Three Classics, one fully sees Anshi's forced interpretations."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "From the Exegesis of the Three Classics one sees how forced Anshi's readings are."

sentences.zh: 淵曰：“穿鑿之過尚小，至於道之大原，安石無一不差。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "The fault of forced interpretation is still small; as to the great root of the Way, Anshi was not once without error.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "Forced reading is a small fault. On the great root of the Way, Anshi missed at every point.

sentences.zh: 推行其學，遂為大害。”

translations.literal: To carry out his learning was to become a great harm."
translations.idiomatic: To impose his learning on the realm was great harm."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“差者何謂？”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In what did he err?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "Where did he err?"

sentences.zh: 淵曰：“聖學所傳止有《論》、《孟》、《中庸》，《論語》主仁，《中庸》主誠，《孟子》主性，安石皆暗其原。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "What the sage learning transmits stops with the Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean—the Analects takes benevolence as its theme, the Mean takes sincerity, Mencius takes nature; Anshi was blind to these roots.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "Sage learning rests on the Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean—the Analects on benevolence, the Mean on sincerity, Mencius on human nature. Anshi was blind to all three.

sentences.zh: 仁道至大，《論語》隨問隨答，惟樊遲問，始對曰：‘愛人。

translations.literal: The Way of benevolence is supremely great; in the Analects, question by question it answers as asked—only when Fan Chi asked did it first reply, 'Love others.'
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence is vast; the Analects answers each question as it comes—only to Fan Chi's question did Confucius first say, 'Love others.'

sentences.zh: ’愛特仁之一端，而安石遂以愛為仁。

translations.literal: ' Love is only one branch of benevolence, yet Anshi took love as benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Love is but one branch of benevolence, yet Anshi made love the whole of benevolence.

sentences.zh: 其言《中庸》，則謂中庸所以接人，高明所以處己。

translations.literal: In speaking of the Mean he said that the mean is for receiving others while loftiness and clarity are for treating oneself.
translations.idiomatic: On the Mean he said the mean is for dealing with others while loftiness is for oneself.

sentences.zh: 《孟子》七篇，專發明性善，而安石取揚雄善惡混之言，至於無善無惡，又溺於佛，其失性遠矣。”

translations.literal: The seven chapters of Mencius specialize in expounding the goodness of nature, yet Anshi took Yang Xiong's saying that good and evil are mixed, even to no good and no evil, and moreover drowned in Buddhism—his loss of nature was far indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius's seven chapters expound the goodness of nature, yet Anshi took Yang Xiong's doctrine that good and evil mix—even to 'neither good nor evil'—and drowned in Buddhism. He lost human nature utterly."

sentences.zh: 鄭億年復資政殿學士、奉朝請，召見於內殿。

translations.literal: Zheng Yinian was again made Academician of the Zizheng Hall and Court Attendant, and summoned to audience in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yinian was restored as Academician of the Zizheng Hall and Court Attendant and summoned to the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 淵言：“億年故相居中之子，雖為從官，而有從賊之醜，乞浸其職名。”

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Yinian is the son of the former chief minister Juzhong; though he is a follower at court, he has the ugliness of having followed the bandits—I beg that his title be gradually reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan objected: "Yinian is the son of the former chief minister Zheng Juzhong. Though he holds court rank, he bears the stain of having served the puppet regime. I beg that his titles be slowly stripped."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not respond.

sentences.zh: 億年，右僕射秦檜之親黨也，由是檜怒之。

translations.literal: Yinian was a kinsman of the Right Vice Director Qin Hui; because of this Hui was angry with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yinian was kin to Vice Director Qin Hui; Hui therefore turned against Yuan.

sentences.zh: 除秘書少監兼崇政殿說書，以祖名辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, but declined on account of his grandfather's name taboo.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Junior Director of the Secretariat and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall but declined because of a name taboo with his grandfather.

sentences.zh: 改宗正少卿，以何鑄論罷。

translations.literal: He was changed to Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Court, but was dismissed on He Zhu's impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Court, then removed on He Zhu's impeachment.

sentences.zh: 主管台州崇道觀。

translations.literal: He was put in charge of the Chongdao Taoist Abbey in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of the Chongdao Taoist Abbey in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 魏矼，字邦達，和州曆陽人，唐丞相知古後也。

translations.literal: Wei Gang, courtesy name Bangda, was a native of Liyang in Hezhou, a descendant of the Tang chief minister Wei Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gang, styled Bangda, came from Liyang in He Prefecture, a descendant of the Tang chief minister Wei Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 少穎悟。

translations.literal: In youth he was sharp and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick and perceptive.

sentences.zh: 時方尚王氏新說，矼獨守所學。

translations.literal: At the time Wang's New Learning was still honored; Gang alone held to his own learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi's New Learning was still in fashion, Gang held to the older learning.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，上舍及第。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe he passed the upper-college examination and received the highest degree.
translations.idiomatic: In 1121 he passed the upper-college examination with highest honors.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，召赴闕，詔改宣教郎，除詳定一司敕令所刪定官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan he was summoned to court; an edict changed his rank to Instructor and appointed him Revising Officer of the Commission for the Revision of Statutes of the One Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1130 he was summoned to court, given the rank Instructor, and made reviser on the Commission for Statutes of the One Office.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，遷樞密院計議官，遷考功郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he was transferred to Planning Officer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then to Director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 he became Planning Officer in the Bureau of Military Affairs, then Director of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 會星變，矼因轉對，言：“治平間，彗出東方，英宗問輔臣所以消弭之道，韓琦以明賞罰為對。

translations.literal: When a comet appeared, Gang took his turn at audience and said: "In the Zhiping period a comet appeared in the east; Emperor Yingzong asked his chief ministers how to dispel and extinguish it, and Han Qi answered with clear rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared, Gang spoke in audience: "Under Emperor Yingzong in the Zhiping era a comet rose in the east. Yingzong asked how to dispel it; Han Qi answered, 'Make rewards and punishments clear.'"

sentences.zh: 比年以來，賞之所加，有未參選而官已升朝者，有未經任而輒為正郎者，罰之所加，有未到任而例被沖替者，有罪犯同而罰有輕重者。”

translations.literal: In recent years among rewards given, some have not yet been selected for office yet already been promoted to court rank; some have not yet served yet already made Regular Gentleman; among punishments given, some have not yet reached their posts yet are routinely displaced; some have the same offense yet unequal penalties."
translations.idiomatic: Today some men are promoted to court rank before they ever enter the selection lists; some become Regular Gentlemen before they ever serve. Some are displaced before they reach their posts; some share the same crime yet receive unequal punishment."

sentences.zh: 力言大臣黜陟不公，所以致異。

translations.literal: He forcefully said that the great ministers' promotions and demotions were not fair, and that this was what brought the prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted that unfair promotions and demotions by the great ministers had brought the omen.

sentences.zh: 上識其忠，擢監察御史，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: The emperor recognized his loyalty and promoted him to Investigating Censor, then Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor recognized his loyalty and made him Investigating Censor, then Attending Censor within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 臨安火，延燒數千家，獻諛者謂非災異。

translations.literal: A fire in Lin'an spread and burned several thousand homes; flatterers said it was not a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Fire in Lin'an burned thousands of homes; flatterers denied it was an omen.

sentences.zh: 矼言：“《春秋》定、哀間數言火災，說者謂孔子有德而魯不能用，季孫有惡而不能去，故天降之咎。

translations.literal: Gang said: "Between the Ding and Ai reigns the Spring and Autumn Annals several times mention fires; commentators hold that Confucius had virtue yet Lu could not employ him, and Ji Sun had evil yet could not be removed—therefore Heaven sent down this blame.
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "The Spring and Autumn Annals records several fires between the reigns of Ding and Ai. Commentators say Confucius had virtue but Lu would not use him; Jisun harbored evil but could not be removed—so Heaven sent fire as blame.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷之上有奸慝邪佞之人未逐乎？

translations.literal: Are there today above the court treacherous, wicked, and flatteringly evil men not yet driven out?
translations.idiomatic: Are there treacherous and flattering men above the court not yet driven out?

sentences.zh: 百執事之間有朋附奔競之徒未汰乎？

translations.literal: Among the hundred executors are there not men of clique-attachment and frantic competition not yet eliminated?
translations.idiomatic: Among the hundred executors, are clique-runners and frantic climbers not yet purged?

sentences.zh: 搢紳有公忠宿望及抱道懷藝、有猷有守之士未用乎？

translations.literal: Among the gentry are there not men of public loyalty, long-standing repute, who embrace the Way and cherish talent, who have plans and hold to principle, not yet employed?
translations.idiomatic: Among the gentry, are men of public loyalty, long repute, learning, and steadfast principle not yet employed?

sentences.zh: 在位之人，畏人軋己，方且蔽賢，未聞推誠盡公，旁招俊乂。

translations.literal: Those in office fear others' pressure on themselves and just now conceal the worthy; they have not been heard to push sincerity to the utmost public good and broadly recruit the outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Men in office fear rivals and hide the worthy; they do not push sincerity, recruit talent broadly, and serve the public good.

sentences.zh: 宜鑒定、哀之失，甄別邪正，亟加進用。”

translations.literal: One should take warning from the errors of Ding and Ai, distinguish the wicked from the upright, and hasten to promote and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Take warning from Ding and Ai: distinguish the wicked from the upright and promote the worthy at once."

sentences.zh: 內侍李暠飲韓世忠家，刃傷弓匠，事下廷尉。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Li Hao drank at Han Shizhong's house and with a blade wounded a bow-maker; the matter went down to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Li Hao drank at Han Shizhong's house and wounded a bow-maker with a blade; the case went to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 矼言：“內侍出入宮禁，而狠戾發於杯酒，乃至如此，豈得不過為之慮？

translations.literal: Gang said: "Inner attendants come and go within the palace precincts, yet from a cup of wine their fierceness and violence broke out to this degree—how can one not go beyond considering this?
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "Eunuchs pass in and out of the palace, yet over wine this man's violence broke out—how can we not take warning?

sentences.zh: 建炎詔令禁內侍不得交通主兵官及預朝政，違者處以軍法。

translations.literal: The Jianyan edict ordered that inner attendants must not associate with commanders of troops or participate in court politics; violators were to be punished by military law.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianyan edict forbade eunuchs to associate with army commanders or join court politics on pain of military law.

sentences.zh: 乞申嚴其禁，以謹履霜之戒。”

translations.literal: I beg that this prohibition be strictly enforced, to heed the warning of treading on hoarfrost."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this ban be enforced strictly, as a warning against the tread on hoarfrost that foretells ice."

sentences.zh: 於是廙杖脊配瓊州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hao was beaten with the cudgel on the spine and banished to Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hao was beaten and banished to Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，賜矼五品服。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor and granted fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was promoted to Attending Censor and granted fifth-rank robes.

sentences.zh: 時朱勝非獨相，矼論：“勝非無所建明，惟知今日進呈一二細故，明日啟擬一二故人，而機務不決，軍政不修，除授挾私，賢士解體。”

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Shengfei alone was chief minister; Gang criticized: "Shengfei has nothing to establish or clarify; he only knows to present one or two trifles today and tomorrow to draft one or two old acquaintances, while critical affairs are not decided, military government is not repaired, appointments carry private favor, and worthy men are disheartened."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shengfei held the chief ministership alone, Gang said, "Shengfei establishes nothing. He presents a trifle today, drafts an old friend tomorrow, leaves critical business undecided, neglects the armies, fills posts by favor, and disheartens the worthy."

sentences.zh: 又疏其五罪，詔令勝非持餘服。

translations.literal: He also memorialized his five offenses; an edict ordered Shengfei to observe the remainder of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He listed five offenses; the court ordered Shengfei to observe the remainder of his mourning leave.

sentences.zh: 又言：“國家命令之出，必先錄黃。

translations.literal: He also said: "When the state's commands go forth, they must first be recorded in yellow.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "State commands must first be recorded on yellow paper.

sentences.zh: 其過兩省，則給捨得以封駁；

translations.literal: When they pass the Two Departments, the drafting recipients may seal and remonstrate;
translations.idiomatic: When they pass the Two Departments, drafting recipients may seal and remonstrate;

sentences.zh: 其下所屬，則台諫得以論列。

translations.literal: when they go down to subordinates, the censors may discuss and lay out objections.
translations.idiomatic: when they reach subordinates, censors may object.

sentences.zh: 此萬世良法也。

translations.literal: This is a good law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: That is a law good for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 竊聞近時三省、樞密院，間有不用錄黃而直降指揮者，亦有雖畫黃而不下六部者，望並依舊制。”

translations.literal: I have heard that recently among the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs there have sometimes been cases of not using the yellow record but directly issuing commands, and also cases of though drafting in yellow yet not sending down to the Six Ministries—I hope all will follow the old system.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that lately the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs sometimes skip the yellow record and issue commands directly, or draft in yellow without sending them to the Six Ministries. I beg that the old procedures be restored."

sentences.zh: 劉豫挾金人入寇，宰相趙鼎決親征之議，矼請扈從，因命督江上諸軍。

translations.literal: Liu Qi, relying on the Jin people, invaded; Chancellor Zhao Ding resolved on the policy of the emperor's personal campaign; Gang requested to accompany the guard and was thereupon ordered to supervise the armies on the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qi invaded with Jin backing, Zhao Ding resolved that Gaozong should take the field in person. Gang asked to accompany the guard and was ordered to supervise the Yangzi armies.

sentences.zh: 時劉光世、韓世忠、張俊三大將權均勢敵，又懷私隙，莫肯協心。

translations.literal: At that time the three great generals Liu Guangshi, Han Shizhong, and Zhang Jun were equal in power and hostile in private grudge, and none would cooperate in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi, Han Shizhong, and Zhang Jun were evenly matched in power and nursed private grudges; none would cooperate.

sentences.zh: 矼首至光世軍中，諭之曰：“賊眾我寡，合力猶懼不支，況軍自為心，將何以戰？

translations.literal: Gang first arrived at Guangshi's army and instructed him: "The bandits are many and we few—even united we still fear we cannot hold; how much less when the armies are each a heart unto itself—how will you fight?
translations.idiomatic: Gang went first to Guangshi's camp and said, "The enemy outnumbers us—even united we may not hold. If each army minds only itself, how will you fight?

sentences.zh: 為諸公計，當思為國雪恥，釋去私隙，不獨有利於國，亦將有利其身。”

translations.literal: For you gentlemen I calculate: you should think on wiping the nation's shame clean, release private grudges, and it will not only benefit the state but also benefit yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Think of wiping the nation's shame clean and dropping private feuds—that helps the state and yourselves alike."

sentences.zh: 光世許之，遂勸其貽書二帥，示以無他，二帥復書交歡。

translations.literal: Guangshi agreed and thereupon urged him to send letters to the two commanders, showing there was no other intent; the two commanders replied in mutual goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi agreed and urged him to write the other commanders pledging good faith; they answered in kind.

sentences.zh: 光世以書聞，由此眾戰屢捷，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Guangshi reported the letters to the court; from this the armies fought repeatedly with success and military renown greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi reported the exchange to court; thereafter the armies won repeated victories and their fame soared.

sentences.zh: 上至平江，魏良臣、王繪使金回，約再遣使，且有恐迫語。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Pingjiang, Wei Liangchen and Wang Hui returned as envoys to the Jin and arranged to send envoys again, and there were also words of intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingjiang, Wei Liangchen and Wang Hui returned from Jin missions proposing further embassies, with words of intimidation.

sentences.zh: 矼請罷“講和”二字，飭厲諸將，力圖攻取。

translations.literal: Gang requested abolishing the two words "discuss peace" and sternly admonishing the generals to strive to attack and recover.
translations.idiomatic: Gang asked that the word "peace" be struck from court discourse and the generals admonished to fight for recovery.

sentences.zh: 會金屢敗遁去，使亦不遣。

translations.literal: When the Jin were repeatedly defeated and fled, the envoys were also not sent.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were beaten back repeatedly; the envoys were never sent.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 矼在職七閱月，論事凡百二十餘章。

translations.literal: In his post for seven months he discussed affairs in more than one hundred twenty memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In seven months in office he submitted more than a hundred twenty memorials.

sentences.zh: 尋乞補外，除直龍圖閣、知泉州，以親老辭，知建州。

translations.literal: Soon he begged an outside appointment and was made Direct Academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Quanzhou; citing aged parents he declined and was made prefect of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked for an outside post and was named Direct Academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Quanzhou; pleading for his parents he declined and was sent to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋召還，丐祠，不允，除權吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled again, begged a Taoist abbey commission and was not granted it, and was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled again, he begged a sinecure without success and was made Acting Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 八年，金使入境，命矼充館伴使，矼言：“頃任御史，嘗論和議之非，今難以專論。”

translations.literal: In the eighth year Jin envoys entered the borders; Gang was ordered to serve as reception commissioner for the embassy; Gang said: "In my former post as censor I once discussed the error of peace talks; today it is hard to speak on this alone."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Jin envoys crossed the border; Gang was ordered to receive them. He said, "As censor I once condemned peace talks; today I cannot argue that case alone."

sentences.zh: 秦檜召矼至都堂，問其所以不主和之意，矼具陳敵情難保，檜諭之曰：“公以智料敵，檜以誠待敵。”

translations.literal: Qin Hui summoned Gang to the Councilors' Hall and asked his reasons for not supporting peace; Gang fully set forth that the enemy's situation was hard to trust; Hui instructed him: "You use wisdom to measure the enemy; I use sincerity to treat the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui summoned him to the Councilors' Hall and asked why he opposed peace. Gang laid out why the enemy could not be trusted. Hui replied, "You measure the enemy with cleverness; I treat the enemy with sincerity."

sentences.zh: 矼曰：“相公固以誠待敵，第恐敵人不以誠待相公耳。”

translations.literal: Gang said: "The chief minister indeed uses sincerity toward the enemy—I only fear the enemy will not use sincerity toward the chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "You may treat them with sincerity—but I fear they will not treat you with sincerity."

sentences.zh: 檜不能屈，乃改命吳表臣。

translations.literal: Hui could not bend him and thereupon changed the appointment to Wu Biaochen.
translations.idiomatic: Hui could not bend him and gave the post to Wu Biaochen instead.

sentences.zh: 詔金使入境，欲屈己就和，令侍從、台諫條奏來上。

translations.literal: An edict said that when Jin envoys entered the borders and the court wished to humble itself for peace, it ordered attendant officials and censors to submit items in writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoys entered the border the throne wished to humble itself for peace and ordered attendants and censors to submit written opinions.

sentences.zh: 矼言：“臣素不熟敵情，不知使人所需者何禮，陛下所以屈己者何事。

translations.literal: Gang said: "Your servant has never been familiar with the enemy's situation and does not know what rites the envoys require, nor what Your Majesty humbles yourself for.
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "I do not know the enemy's mind, what rites their envoys demand, or what Your Majesty would humble yourself to grant.

sentences.zh: 賊豫為金人所立，為之北面，陛下承祖宗基業，天命所歸，何藉于金國乎？

translations.literal: The bandit Qi was established by the Jin people; he faces north for them—Your Majesty inherits the ancestral foundation and the mandate of Heaven—what need have you of the Jin state?
translations.idiomatic: The puppet Liu Qi was set up by the Jin and bows north to them. Your Majesty inherits the ancestral foundation and Heaven's mandate—why lean on the Jin?

sentences.zh: 傳聞奉使之歸，謂金人悉從我所欲，必無難行之禮，以重困我，陛下何過自取侮乎？

translations.literal: It is rumored that when the mission returns they will say the Jin entirely grant what we desire and there will surely be no hard rites, yet to heavily burden us—why should Your Majesty go beyond and invite insult?
translations.idiomatic: Rumor says the returning envoys will claim the Jin grant everything we ask, with no hard terms—yet they will burden us. Why invite insult?

sentences.zh: 如或不可從之事，儻輕許之，他時反為所制，號令廢置將出其手，一有不從，便生兵隙。

translations.literal: If there are matters that cannot be followed and one lightly promises them, later one will be controlled by them; orders of abolition and appointment will issue from their hands—once there is one refusal, military strife will arise.
translations.idiomatic: If we lightly promise what we cannot keep, they will control us—appointments and dismissals will issue from their hands; one refusal and war follows.

sentences.zh: 予奪在彼，失信在我，非計之得也。

translations.literal: Granting and taking away will be in their hands; loss of trust will be in ours—this is not a winning plan.
translations.idiomatic: They would hold the power of grant and denial; we would hold the loss of trust—that is no winning plan.

sentences.zh: 雖使還我空地，如之何而可保？

translations.literal: Even if they return our empty lands, how can they be secured?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they return empty territory, how could we hold it?

sentences.zh: 雖欲寢兵，如之何而可寢？

translations.literal: Even if we wish to rest the armies, how can they be rested?
translations.idiomatic: Even if we wished to rest the armies, how could they rest?

sentences.zh: 雖欲息民，如之何而可息？

translations.literal: Even if we wish to ease the people, how can they be eased?
translations.idiomatic: Even if we wished to ease the people, how could they be eased?

sentences.zh: 非計之得也。

translations.literal: This is not a winning plan.
translations.idiomatic: That is no winning plan.

sentences.zh: 陛下既欲為親少屈，更願審思天下治亂之機，酌之群情，擇其經久可行者行之，其不可從者，以國人之意拒之，庶無後悔。
