translations.literal: Your Majesty already wishes to humble yourself slightly for kinship—further I beg careful thought on the mechanisms of order and disorder under Heaven, weigh them against popular feeling, carry out what can long be practiced, and for what cannot be followed, reject it with the will of the people of the state—then there will be no later regret.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will bend slightly for kinship, weigh order and disorder, heed popular feeling, do what can last, and reject what the nation cannot bear with the people's will—there will be no regret.

sentences.zh: 所謂國人者，不過萬民、三軍爾。

translations.literal: What is called the people of the state is nothing beyond the myriad people and the Three Armies.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the state are the myriad people and the Three Armies.

sentences.zh: 搢紳與萬民一體，大將與三軍一體，今陛下詢于搢紳，民情大可見矣。

translations.literal: The gentry and the myriad people are one body; the great generals and the Three Armies are one body—now Your Majesty inquires of the gentry, and popular feeling is already plain.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and people are one body; great generals and armies are one body. Your Majesty has asked the gentry—the people's will is plain.

sentences.zh: 欲望速召大將，各帶近上統制官數人同來，詳加訪問，以塞他日意外之憂。

translations.literal: I desire quickly to summon the great generals, each bringing several officers of close command from the court, to come together and inquire in detail, to block unexpected worry on another day.
translations.idiomatic: Summon the great generals at once, each with several close commanders, question them in detail, and forestall future surprise.

sentences.zh: 大將以為不可，則其氣益堅，何憂此敵。”

translations.literal: If the great generals say it cannot be done, then their spirit will be the firmer—why fear this enemy?
translations.idiomatic: If the generals say peace is impossible, their spirit will harden—why fear the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 免喪，除集英殿修撰、知宣州，不就。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Talents and prefect of Xuanzhou but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was named Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Talents and prefect of Xuanzhou but did not go.

sentences.zh: 改提舉太平興國宮，自是奉祠，凡四任。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commissioner for the Taiping Xingguo Palace, and from this served in Taoist abbey posts for four terms in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to oversee the Taiping Xingguo Palace and held abbey commissions four times in all.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱以卒。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother and died in the course of it.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother and died during it.

sentences.zh: 潘良貴

translations.literal: Pan Lianggui
translations.idiomatic: Pan Lianggui

sentences.zh: 潘良貴，字子賤，婺州金華人。

translations.literal: Pan Lianggui, courtesy name Zijian, was a native of Jinhua in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Lianggui, styled Zijian, was from Jinhua in Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以上舍釋褐為辟雍博士，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: Through the upper college he was released from service obligations and made Erudite of the Imperial University, then transferred to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Through the upper college he entered service as Erudite of the Imperial University, then became a Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時宰相蔡京與其子攸方以爵祿鉤知名士，良貴屹然特立，親故數為京致願交意，良貴正色謝絕。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Minister Cai Jing and his son You were using ranks and salaries to hook famous scholars; Lianggui stood upright and alone, and relatives and friends several times conveyed Jing's wish to associate—Lianggui with stern countenance refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing and his son You used rank and salary to hook famous scholars, Lianggui stood alone. Relatives repeatedly conveyed Jing's wish to befriend him; Lianggui refused with a stern face.

sentences.zh: 除主客郎中，尋提舉淮南東路常平。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Bureau of Receptions, and soon Commissioner for the Huainan East Circuit Ever-Normal Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Bureau of Receptions, then Commissioner for the Huainan East Ever-Normal Granary.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，召還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 賜對，欽宗問孰可秉鈞軸者，良貴極言：“何㮚、唐恪等四人不可用，他日必誤社稷。

translations.literal: Granted audience, when Emperor Qinzong asked who could hold the chief ministership, Lianggui spoke forcefully: "He Li, Tang Ke, and the other four cannot be used; one day they will surely mislead the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: In audience, Qinzong asked who could hold the chief ministership. Lianggui said bluntly, "He Li, Tang Ke, and four others cannot be used; they will one day ruin the state.

sentences.zh: 陛下若欲扶危持顛之相，非博詢於下僚，明揚於微陋，未見其可。”

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes a chief minister to support peril and hold up collapse, unless you broadly inquire among lower officials and clearly raise men from obscurity, I do not see one who can do it."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wants a minister to save a tottering realm, you must search broadly among lower officials and raise the obscure—I see no other way."

sentences.zh: 語徹於外，當國者指為狂率，黜監信州汭口排岸。

translations.literal: The words reached outside; those holding power called him reckless and demoted him to Supervisor of the Ruikou Wharf at Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His words leaked out. Those in power called him reckless and demoted him to supervisor of the Ruikou wharf in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 越數年，除提點荊湖南路刑獄，主管江州太平觀，除考功郎，遷左司。

translations.literal: After several years he was appointed Commissioner for Punishments in the Jingnan South Circuit, put in charge of the Taiping Taoist Abbey in Jiangzhou, made Director of the Bureau of Appointments, and transferred to the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was made Punishments Commissioner for Jingnan South, overseer of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou, Director of the Bureau of Appointments, then Left Office director.

sentences.zh: 宰相呂頤浩從容謂良貴曰：“旦夕相引入兩省。”

translations.literal: Chief Minister Lü Yihao said to Lianggui at ease: "Soon the chief minister will introduce you into the Two Departments."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Lü Yihao said casually, "Soon I will bring you into the Two Departments."

sentences.zh: 良貴正色對曰：“親老方欲乞外，兩省官非良貴可為也。”

translations.literal: Lianggui with stern countenance replied: "My parents are aged and I was just about to beg an outside post—the offices of the Two Departments are not what Lianggui can fill."
translations.idiomatic: Lianggui answered sternly, "My parents are old and I was about to beg an outside post. The Two Departments are not for me."

sentences.zh: 退語人曰：“宰相進退一世人才，以為賢邪，自當擢用，何可握手密語，先示私恩。

translations.literal: Retiring he told others: "The chief minister advances and dismisses the talent of a generation—if he thinks one worthy, he should promote him on his own; how can he clasp hands in secret talk and first show private favor?
translations.idiomatic: He told others afterward, "A chief minister advances the talent of a generation. If he thinks a man worthy, let him promote him openly—why clasp hands in secret and show private favor first?

sentences.zh: 若士大夫受其牢籠，又何以立朝。”

translations.literal: If scholar-officials accept his cage, how can they stand at court?"
translations.idiomatic: If scholar-officials accept such snares, how can they stand at court?"

sentences.zh: 即日乞補外，以直龍圖閣知嚴州。

translations.literal: That same day he begged an outside post and was made Direct Academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That day he begged an outside post and was made Direct Academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 到官兩月，請祠，主管亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: Two months after reaching his post he requested an abbey commission and was put in charge of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Two months after arrival he asked for an abbey post and was put in charge of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 起為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was raised to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 會戶部侍郎向子諲入見，語言煩褻，良貴故善子諲，是日攝起居，立殿上，徑至榻前厲聲曰：“子諲以無益之談久煩聖聽！”

translations.literal: When Vice Minister of Revenue Xiang Ziyin entered for audience his speech was tedious and improper; Lianggui had formerly been on good terms with Ziyin; that day he was acting Gentleman Attendant, standing on the hall, and went straight to the couch before the throne and in a stern voice said: "Ziyin with useless talk has long troubled the sage ear!"
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Xiang Ziyin spoke at audience his talk was tedious and improper. Lianggui, who had been friendly with him, was acting Gentleman Attendant that day. He strode to the throne and said sharply, "Ziyin has long troubled the imperial ear with useless talk!"

sentences.zh: 子諲欲退，高宗顧良貴曰：“是朕問之。”

translations.literal: Ziyin wished to withdraw; Emperor Gaozong turned to Lianggui and said: "It was I who asked him."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyin tried to withdraw. Gaozong told Lianggui, "I asked him."

sentences.zh: 又諭子諲且款語。

translations.literal: He again instructed Ziyin to speak at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He told Ziyin to continue at ease.

sentences.zh: 子諲復語，久不止，良貴叱之退者再。

translations.literal: Ziyin spoke again and long did not stop; Lianggui twice shouted at him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyin spoke on and would not stop; Lianggui twice ordered him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 高宗色變，閣門並彈之，於是二人俱待罪。

translations.literal: The emperor's countenance changed; the Gate Department together impeached them, and thereupon both men awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face changed; the Gate Department impeached both, and both awaited punishment.

sentences.zh: 有旨良貴放罪，子諲無罪可待。

translations.literal: An order released Lianggui from guilt; for Ziyin there was no guilt to await.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggui was released; Ziyin had no case to answer.

sentences.zh: 良貴求去，以集英殿修撰提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Lianggui requested leave and was made Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Talents overseeing the Taiping Taoist Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggui asked to leave and was made Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Talents overseeing the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 起知明州。

translations.literal: He was raised to prefect of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to prefect of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 期年，除徽猷閣待制、提舉亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: After the term he was made Awaiting Draft at the Huaiyou Pavilion and Commissioner for the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his term he was made Awaiting Draft at the Huaiyou Pavilion and Commissioner for the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 既歸，不出者十年。

translations.literal: Once home he did not go out for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Once home he did not go out for ten years.

sentences.zh: 李光得罪，良貴坐嘗與通書，降三官。

translations.literal: When Li Guang was punished, Lianggui was demoted three ranks on the charge of having once exchanged letters with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guang fell, Lianggui was demoted three ranks for having once exchanged letters with him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 良貴剛介清苦，壯老一節。

translations.literal: Lianggui was firm, independent, pure, and austere; from youth to old age one integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggui was firm, independent, pure, and austere—one integrity from youth to age.

sentences.zh: 為博士時，王黼、張邦昌俱欲妻以女，拒之。

translations.literal: When he was an erudite, Wang Fu and Zhang Bangchang both wished to marry daughters to him; he refused.
translations.idiomatic: As erudite, Wang Fu and Zhang Bangchang both wished him to marry their daughters; he refused.

sentences.zh: 晚家居貧甚，秦檜諷令求郡，良貴曰：“從臣除授合辭免，今求之于宰相，辭之于君父，良貴不敢為也。”

translations.literal: In his later years he lived at home in extreme poverty; Qin Hui hinted that he should request a prefecture; Lianggui said: "Followers at court receiving appointment ought to decline; now to request from the chief minister and decline before the ruler and father—I dare not do it."
translations.idiomatic: In old age he lived in deep poverty. Qin Hui hinted he should ask for a prefecture. Lianggui said, "Court followers should decline appointment. To beg a chief minister and then decline before the throne—I dare not."

sentences.zh: 其諫疏多焚稿，僅存雜著十五卷，新安朱熹為之序。

translations.literal: Many of his remonstrance memorials were burned as drafts; only miscellaneous writings in fifteen scrolls survive, for which Zhu Xi of Xin'an wrote a preface.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his memorials were burned as drafts; only fifteen scrolls of miscellany survive, prefaced by Zhu Xi of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 呂本中

translations.literal: Lu Benzhong
translations.idiomatic: Lu Benzhong

sentences.zh: 呂本中，字居仁，元祐宰相公著之曾孫、好問之子。

translations.literal: Lu Benzhong, courtesy name Juren, was the great-grandson of the Yuanyou chief minister Lu Gongzhu and the son of Haowen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Benzhong, styled Juren, was the great-grandson of Yuanyou chief minister Lu Gongzhu and son of Haowen.

sentences.zh: 幼而敏悟，公著奇愛之。

translations.literal: In youth he was sharp and perceptive; Gongzhu marveled at and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was quick and perceptive; Gongzhu doted on him.

sentences.zh: 公著薨，宣仁太后及哲宗臨奠，諸童稚立庭下，宣仁獨進本中，摩其頭曰：“孝於親，忠於君，兒勉焉。”

translations.literal: When Gongzhu died, Empress Dowager Xuanren and Emperor Zhezong came to mourn; the children stood below the courtyard; Xuanren alone advanced Benzhong, stroked his head, and said: "Filial toward kin, loyal toward the ruler—child, strive on.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongzhu died, Empress Xuanren and Zhezong came to mourn. Children stood in the courtyard; Xuanren alone drew Benzhong forward, stroked his head, and said, "Be filial to kin, loyal to your ruler—strive, child."

sentences.zh: 祖希哲師程頤，本中聞見習熟。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xizhe studied under Cheng Yi; Benzhong heard and saw until familiar.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xizhe studied under Cheng Yi; Benzhong grew up steeped in that world.

sentences.zh: 少長，從楊時、游酢、尹焞遊，三家或有疑異，未嘗苟同。

translations.literal: Growing up he followed Yang Shi, You Zuo, and Yin Huan in study; among the three houses there were sometimes doubts and differences, yet he never agreed lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with Yang Shi, You Zuo, and Yin Huan; when the three houses differed, he never agreed lightly.

sentences.zh: 以公著遺表恩，授承務郎。

translations.literal: On the grace of Gongzhu's final memorial he was given the rank of Assistant Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: On the grace of Gongzhu's final memorial he received the rank Assistant Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement.

sentences.zh: 紹聖間，黨事起，公著追貶，本中坐焉。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng period, when factional affairs arose, Gongzhu was posthumously demoted and Benzhong was implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When factional purges began in Shaosheng, Gongzhu was posthumously demoted and Benzhong was implicated.

sentences.zh: 元符中，主濟陰簿、秦州士曹掾，辟大名府帥司幹官。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfu period he served as registrar of Jiyin, clerical officer for scholars in Qin Prefecture, and staff officer on the headquarters of the Daming prefectural command.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanfu he served as registrar of Jiyin, scholars' clerk in Qin Prefecture, and staff officer at Daming headquarters.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年，除樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanhe he was appointed Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xuanhe he was made Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 靖康改元，遷職方員外郎，以父嫌奉祠。

translations.literal: When Jingkang changed the reign title he was transferred to Outer Director of the Bureau of Appointments and, on account of his father's taboo, given a Taoist abbey commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jingkang reign change he was made Outer Director of the Bureau of Appointments, then given an abbey post on account of his father's taboo.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，召為祠部員外郎，以疾告去。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended and the mourning garment was removed, he was summoned as Outer Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices; citing illness he reported leave.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned as Outer Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices but pleaded illness and left.

sentences.zh: 再直秘閣，主管崇道觀。

translations.literal: He again served at the Secret Repository and was put in charge of the Chongdao Taoist Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He again served at the Secret Repository and oversaw the Chongdao Taoist Abbey.

sentences.zh: 紹興六年，召赴行在，特賜進士出身，擢起居舍人兼權中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shaoxing he was summoned to the mobile court, specially granted jinshi standing, and promoted to Gentleman Attendant with concurrent Acting Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shaoxing he was summoned to court, granted jinshi standing, and made Gentleman Attendant with concurrent Acting Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 內侍李琮失料曆，上以潛邸舊人，不用保任特給之。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Li Cong lost his calendar of duties; because he was an old man of the Hidden Residence, the emperor, without using the guarantee procedure, specially granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Li Cong lost his duty roster; as an old man of Gaozong's princely household, the Emperor granted a replacement without the usual guarantee.

sentences.zh: 本中言：“若以異恩別給，非所謂‘宮中府中當為一體’者。”

translations.literal: Benzhong said: "If by special favor one grants separately, this is not what is called 'within the palace and within the government one should be a single body.'"
translations.idiomatic: Benzhong said, "To grant by special favor is not what the ancients meant by 'palace and government as one body.'"

sentences.zh: 上見繳還，甚悅，令宰臣諭之曰：“自今有所見，第言之。”

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing it returned, was very pleased and ordered the chief ministers to instruct him: "From now on, whatever you see, just speak it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, pleased that he returned the order, told the chief ministers to say to him, "From now on speak whatever you see."

sentences.zh: 監階州草場苗亙以贓敗，有詔從黥，本中奏：“近歲官吏犯贓，多至黥籍，然四方之遠，或有枉濫，何由盡知？

translations.literal: Miao Gen, overseer of the Jie Prefecture fodder grounds, failed through corruption; there was an edict to follow tattooing; Benzhong memorialized: "In recent years officials who corrupt are many tattooed, yet in distant regions there may be wrongful cases—how can one know them all?
translations.idiomatic: Miao Gen, overseer of the Jie fodder grounds, was convicted of corruption; an edict ordered tattooing. Benzhong memorialized, "Lately corrupt officials are often tattooed, yet in distant places wrongful cases may hide—how can we know them all?

sentences.zh: 異時察其非辜，雖欲抆拭，其可得乎？

translations.literal: Another time if one examines that they are not guilty, though one wishes to wipe it clean, how can it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: If later we find them innocent, how wipe the mark away?

sentences.zh: 若祖宗以來此刑嘗用，則紹聖權臣當國之時，士大夫無遺類久矣。

translations.literal: If from the ancestors onward this punishment had been used, then in the Shaosheng period when factional ministers held the state, scholar-officials would long ago have been without survivors.
translations.idiomatic: If our ancestors had used this punishment routinely, no scholar-official would have survived the Shaosheng factional reign.

sentences.zh: 願酌處常罰，毋令奸臣得以藉口於後世。”

translations.literal: I hope to weigh and apply the regular punishments and not let treacherous ministers be able to use it as a pretext in later ages."
translations.idiomatic: Apply the regular punishments and do not let treacherous ministers of later ages use tattooing as a pretext."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his memorial.

sentences.zh: 七年，上幸建康，本中奏曰：“當今之計，必先為恢復事業，求人才，恤民隱，講明法度，詳審刑政，開直言之路，俾人人得以盡情。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor visited Jiankang; Benzhong memorialized: "The plan of today must first establish the work of restoration, seek talent, comfort the people's hardships, clarify laws, examine punishments in detail, open the road of forthright speech, and let every man fully express his mind.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Emperor visited Jiankang, Benzhong memorialized: "Today's plan must first build restoration: seek talent, ease the people's burdens, clarify law, tighten justice, open the road of blunt speech so every man may speak his mind.

sentences.zh: 然後練兵謀帥，增師上流，固守淮甸，使江南先有不可動之勢，伺彼有釁，一舉可克。

translations.literal: Then train troops and plan commanders, increase armies on the upper river, firmly guard the Huai region, so that south of the Yangzi there is first an posture that cannot be moved, watch for their openings, and one stroke can overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Then train troops and choose commanders, strengthen the upper Yangzi armies, hold the Huai firm, make the south unshakable, watch for enemy openings, and strike when the moment comes.

sentences.zh: 若徒有恢復之志，而無其策，邦本未強，恐生他患。

translations.literal: If one has only the will to restore yet lacks the policies, the foundation of the state is not yet strong—I fear other troubles will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Restoration zeal without policy leaves the foundation weak—I fear other troubles will follow.

sentences.zh: 今江南、兩浙科須日繁，閭裡告病，倘有水旱乏絕，奸宄竊發，未審朝廷何以待之？

translations.literal: Now in Jiangnan and the Two Zhe circuits the tax levies grow daily; villages report distress—if drought or flood brings want, and treacherous villains rise in secret, I do not know how the court will meet it?
translations.idiomatic: Taxes in Jiangnan and the Two Zhes grow daily; villages report distress. If drought or flood brings want and villains stir, how will the court meet it?

sentences.zh: 近者臣庶勸興師問罪者，不可勝數，觀其辭固甚順，考其實不可行。

translations.literal: Recently subjects urging raising armies and inquiring into guilt have been beyond counting; viewing their words they are certainly very compliant, but examining their substance they cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Lately subjects urging war are beyond count; their words sound loyal, their plans cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 大抵獻言之人，與朝廷利害絕不相侔，言不酬，事不濟，則脫身而去。

translations.literal: Generally those who offer words and the court's benefit and harm are absolutely not of the same measure—if words are not rewarded and affairs do not succeed, they slip away bodily.
translations.idiomatic: Such men share nothing with the court's interest—if their words fail and plans collapse, they slip away.

sentences.zh: 朝廷施設失當，誰任其咎？

translations.literal: If the court's arrangements are wrongly set, who bears the blame?
translations.idiomatic: If the court misarranges affairs, who bears the blame?

sentences.zh: 鷙鳥將擊，必匿其形，今朝廷於進取未有秋毫之實，所下詔命，已傳賊境，使之得以為備，非策也。”

translations.literal: When the fierce bird is about to strike it must hide its form; now the court in advancing has not the slightest reality, yet the edicts issued have already reached the enemy borders and let them prepare—this is not a policy."
translations.idiomatic: A striking hawk hides its form; yet we advance without real strength while edicts reach the enemy and teach them to prepare—that is no policy."

sentences.zh: 又奏：“江左形勢如九江、鄂渚、荊南諸路，當宿重兵，臨以重臣。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The posture of the left of the river such as Jiujiang, Ezhou, and Jingnan and other routes should lodge heavy troops and be overseen by weighty ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Key points such as Jiujiang, Ezhou, and Jingnan need heavy garrisons and weighty overseers.

sentences.zh: 吳時謂西陵、建平，國之藩表，願精擇守帥，以待緩急，則江南自守之計備矣。”

translations.literal: In Wu times they called Xiling and Jianping the outer screens of the state—I hope to select guarding commanders with care to await urgency and ease, and then the south's plan of self-defense will be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Wu called Xiling and Jianping the realm's outer screens. Choose guarding commanders with care for sudden need, and Jiangnan's defense will be complete."

sentences.zh: 內侍鄭諶落致仕，得兵官。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Zheng Chen was dismissed from retirement and obtained a military post.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zheng Chen left retirement and received a military post.

sentences.zh: 本中言：“陛下進臨江滸，將以有為，今賢士大夫未能顯用，岩穴幽隱未能招致，乃起諶以統兵之任，何邪？”

translations.literal: Benzhong said: "Your Majesty advances to the river's edge intending to accomplish something—now worthy scholar-officials are not yet prominently employed, hidden men of the cliffs and caves are not yet recruited, yet you raise Chen to a post commanding troops—what is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Benzhong said, "Your Majesty comes to the river intending great deeds, yet worthy men are not employed, recluses are not summoned—and you raise Chen to command troops. What is this?"

sentences.zh: 命遂寢。

translations.literal: The order thereupon lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment lapsed.

sentences.zh: 引疾乞祠，直龍圖閣、知台州，不就，主管太平觀。

translations.literal: Citing illness he begged an abbey commission; he was made Direct Academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Taizhou but did not go, and was put in charge of the Taiping Taoist Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Pleading illness he begged an abbey post; named prefect of Taizhou he did not go and oversaw the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 召為太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Junior Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Junior Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he became Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 三月，兼侍講。

translations.literal: In the third month he was concurrently Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was made Lecturer as well.

sentences.zh: 六月，兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was concurrently Acting Academician of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was Acting Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 金使通和，有司議行人之供，本中言：“使人之來，正當示以儉約，客館芻粟若務充悅，適啟戎心。

translations.literal: When Jin envoys came for peace the relevant offices discussed supplies for the envoys; Benzhong said: "When envoys come one should just show austerity; if the guest lodges' fodder and grain are made full to please, that opens the enemy's heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoys came for peace, offices debated their supplies. Benzhong said, "Show austerity to envoys; filling guest lodges only whets enemy appetite.

sentences.zh: 且成敗大計，初不在此，在吾治政得失，兵財強弱，願詔有司令無乏可也。”

translations.literal: Moreover success and failure in the great plan at first do not lie in this—it lies in whether our governance gains or loses, whether armies and wealth are strong or weak; I hope to order the relevant offices to see that there is no lack only.
translations.idiomatic: Victory does not lie in lavish hosting but in governance, armies, and wealth. Order the offices to supply only what is needed, no more."

sentences.zh: 初，本中與秦檜同為郎，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Earlier Benzhong and Qin Hui had been colleagues as bureau directors and got on very well.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Benzhong and Qin Hui had been bureau colleagues and were close friends.

sentences.zh: 檜既相，私有引用，本中封還除目，檜勉其書行，卒不從。

translations.literal: After Hui became chief minister he privately wished to employ him; Benzhong returned the appointment documents sealed; Hui urged him to sign and execute but in the end he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui became chief minister he wished to employ Benzhong privately; Benzhong returned appointment documents sealed; Hui urged him to sign, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎素主元祐之學，謂本中公著後，又範沖所薦，故深相知。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding had always upheld Yuanyou learning and held that Benzhong, as Gongzhu's descendant and also recommended by Fan Chong, therefore deeply knew and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding upheld Yuanyou learning and, knowing Benzhong as Gongzhu's descendant and Fan Chong's protégé, trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 會《哲宗實錄》成，鼎遷僕射，本中草制，有曰：“合晉、楚之成，不若尊王而賤霸；

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Zhezong were completed Ding was transferred to Vice Director; Benzhong drafted the edict, which had the words: "Joining Jin and Chu is not as good as honoring the king and slighting the hegemons;
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Zhezong were completed, Ding was made Vice Director; Benzhong drafted the edict: "Joining Jin and Chu is not as good as honoring the king and slighting hegemons;

sentences.zh: 散牛李之黨，未如明是以去非。”

translations.literal: scattering the Niu and Li factions is not as good as clarifying right to remove wrong."
translations.idiomatic: scattering the Niu and Li factions is not as good as clarifying right to remove wrong."

sentences.zh: 檜大怒，言於上曰：“本中受鼎風旨，伺和議不成，為脫身之計。”

translations.literal: Hui was greatly angered and said to the emperor: "Benzhong received Ding's secret instructions, watching for peace talks to fail as a plan to slip away bodily."
translations.idiomatic: Hui was furious and told the Emperor, "Benzhong took Ding's secret cue, hoping peace would fail so he could slip away."

sentences.zh: 風御史蕭振劾罷之。

translations.literal: He had the censor Xiao Zhen impeach and dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: He had censor Xiao Zhen impeach and dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 提舉太平觀，卒。

translations.literal: Commissioner for the Taiping Taoist Abbey—he died.
translations.idiomatic: As Commissioner for the Taiping Taoist Abbey he died.

sentences.zh: 學者稱為東萊先生，賜諡文清。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Donglai; he was given the posthumous title Wénqīng.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars called him Master Donglai; he was posthumously titled Wénqīng.

sentences.zh: 有詩二十卷得黃庭堅陳師道句法，《春秋解》一十卷、《童蒙訓》三卷、《師友淵源錄》五卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had twenty scrolls of poetry attaining the phrasing of Huang Tingjian and Chen Shidao, ten scrolls of Exegesis of the Spring and Autumn Annals, three scrolls of Instructions for the Young, and five scrolls of Record of Teachers and Friends' Origins, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left twenty scrolls of poetry in the manner of Huang Tingjian and Chen Shidao, ten scrolls of Exegesis of the Spring and Autumn Annals, three of Instructions for the Young, and five of Record of Teachers and Friends—all in circulation.

sentences.zh: 論曰：《傳》有之：“不有君子，其何能國。”

translations.literal: The discussion says: The Documents has it: "Without gentlemen, how could there be a state?"
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: The Documents says, "Without gentlemen, how could there be a state?"

sentences.zh: 紹興之世，呂頤浩、秦檜在相位，雖有君子，豈得盡其志，宋之不能圖復中原，雖曰天命，豈非人事乎？

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era, Lü Yihao and Qin Hui held the chief ministership—though there were gentlemen, how could they fully realize their aims? That Song could not plan to recover the Central Plain—though it is called Heaven's mandate, was it not also human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing, Lü Yihao and Qin Hui held power—even with gentlemen present, how could they fully realize their aims? That Song could not recover the north—though called Heaven's mandate, was it not also human failure?

sentences.zh: 若常同、張致遠、薛徽言、陳淵、魏矼、潘良貴、呂本中，其才猷皆可以經邦，其風節皆可以厲世，然皆論議不合，奉祠去國，可為永慨矣。

translations.literal: Men such as Chang Tong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Xue Huiyan, Chen Yuan, Wei Gang, Pan Lianggui, and Lu Benzhong—their talents could all order the state, their integrity could all steel the age—yet all were at odds in deliberation, took abbey commissions, and left the realm—a lasting grief.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Xue Huiyan, Chen Yuan, Wei Gang, Pan Lianggui, and Lu Benzhong—all had talent to order the state and integrity to steel the age—yet all clashed in council, took abbey posts, and left the realm. That is a lasting grief.
